children: *Currys Comfortable With Market Consensus for The Yr
*Currys Targeting Continued Growth in Higher Margin, Recurring Services Rev
*Currys Sees Yr End Net Cash Well Above GBP100M Target
Currys Reports Strong Start to Fiscal Year
Currys said it had a strong start to its fiscal year as group revenue rose on sales growth across its segments.
The British electronics retailer said Thursday that group like-for-like revenue for the 17 weeks through Aug. 29  rose 7% on year.
Like-for-like revenue in the U.K. and Ireland rose 6%, driven by sales growth both in stores and online, with  double-digit growth in new categories and business-to-business.

Recurring services revenue in the region grew strongly as customers chose flexible payment options--which accounted for 24% of sales--and its iD Mobile network grew its user base by 16% to top 2.7 million subscribers.

In the Nordics region, like-for-like revenue was up 9%, boosted by white goods and mobile, with continued success in new categories, business-to-business and services, Currys said. The retailer made market-share gains in most countries and categories, in a market that saw strong growth against a soft comparative, it said.
The board said it was planning confidently for the remainder of the year, and left its guidance unchanged.

The company is comfortable with market consensus for fiscal 2027, it said.  Company-compiled adjusted pretax profit consensus stands at 199 million pounds ($269.6 million) with adjusted revenue of 9.52 billion pounds. For fiscal 2026 the company reported adjusted pretax profit of 191 million pounds on adjusted revenue of 9.25 billion pounds.
